correctness.rationale: For each of the 256 Wolfram radius-one binary maps, finite spatial image words are exactly labels of paths in a 4-pair-state de Bruijn transducer. Determinization from all four initial states to reachable nonempty subsets (<=15) counts every output block once, so a(n)=e_initial^T A^n 1. Accessibility and nonnegative Perron–Frobenius theory yield exp(h)=rho(A); all row sums <=2. Independent Python/SymPy exact reconstruction built all 256 matrices and characteristic polynomials, used rational Sturm root counts in 19 pairwise-disjoint intervals and exact factor divisibility to identify every Perron class. The class counts are [30,4,4,8,8,4,8,8,4,4,28,44,16,8,8,32,28,8,2]; highest proper class is rules 22,104,151,233, runner-up 37,91,164,218, zero class 0 and 255. Independent input-block enumeration agreed with deterministic counts at 1536 finite (rule,n) pairs. Actual source CSVs were independently fetched by Git blob and inspected as 20 and 257 rows, including exact rational brackets and characteristic polynomials. The infinite word-length entropy is from the matrix-growth proof, not finite samples.
residual_risks: The exact finite certificate covers 256 rules, not larger radii/alphabet; the asymptotic entropy relies on the automaton/Perron argument. No claim on temporal dynamical entropy or finite-ring Shannon entropy.

None of the materially inspected results evaluates all 19 one-step spatial-image entropies with exact isolated Perron roots and global Rule-22 four-rule optimum. Older entropy rankings based on Shannon time-series or asynchronous update are different metrics. Resultary queried the all-256 one-step image problem and returned temporal automata and specific-rule dynamics rather than complete spectrum. A prior unindexed 256-rule subset-automata table remains a real novelty risk.
